progressionAssessment.rationale: The life-science gateway precedes anatomy, cell biology, physiology, laboratory work and advanced biomedical courses. The brain and behaviour gateway precedes advanced cognition and psychology. Introductory research design and statistics lead into experimental methods and evidence synthesis.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One related programme combines biomedical science, prevention, health behaviour and evidence appraisal. An oral-science or clinical dentistry option would require a sustained sequence in oral anatomy, dental disease, preclinical techniques, treatment planning and supervised patient care.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce cellular and molecular foundations of human health. Groningen develops these foundations within dental training.
Both develop knowledge of normal bodily function. UCR focuses on adult organ systems and homeostasis.
Both draw on mechanisms of infection and immunity to explain compromised health. Groningen applies these concepts in oral healthcare.
Both consider how disease mechanisms affect health. The UCR cases concern systemic disease and clinical reasoning across organ systems.
Both address prevention. UCR studies disease patterns, risk and interventions at population level. Groningen applies prevention to oral health.
Both examine how behaviour and social context shape health and care. UCR includes interviews and general medical settings. Groningen uses oral-health cases.
Both consider how development and behaviour change across life stages. Groningen applies this to dental growth and care.
Both introduce scientific inquiry. UCR adds a team project that collects and analyses data.
Both develop empirical research skills. UCR focuses on experimental design and multivariable analysis.
Both evaluate and synthesise research. UCR teaches systematic review and meta-analysis. Groningen requires an individual supervised bachelor thesis in dentistry.
Both include reflection on professional development. UCR develops academic writing, self-management and civic engagement.

notes.text: The UCR option shares foundations in human biology, prevention, health behaviour and research. Groningen also requires oral anatomy and disease science, dental materials and radiography, preclinical skills, treatment planning and supervised patient care. The UCR option does not lead to qualification as a dentist.

audience.programmeDescription: Dentistry at the University of Groningen combines human and oral science with technical skills and patient care. Students practise on artificial jaws and teeth, progress to supervised care and complete a bachelor thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in human biology, disease, prevention and health behaviour. Groningen builds on these foundations with dental diagnosis, restorative techniques and supervised treatment.
